primary.title: The Life of Saladin
primary.author: Baha al-Din ibn Shaddad
primary.rationale: This is a contemporary biography of Saladin, written by his chief judge and companion. While not authored by Saladin himself, it is considered a primary source due to its direct access to Saladin and his court.

secondary.title: Saladin: The Sultan Who Forged an Empire
secondary.author: John Man
secondary.rationale: A comprehensive and well-regarded biography of Saladin, drawing on extensive research and providing modern scholarly analysis.

secondary.title: The Crusades: The Authoritative History of the War for the Holy Land
secondary.author: Thomas Asbridge
secondary.rationale: While covering the broader Crusades, this book offers significant and scholarly analysis of Saladin's role and impact within the context of the period.

secondary.title: Saladin and the Fall of Jerusalem
secondary.author: Charles Frazee
secondary.rationale: A scholarly examination of Saladin's life and military campaigns, focusing on his pivotal role in the recapture of Jerusalem.

suggestions.notes: Direct primary sources authored by Saladin are scarce and often exist only in fragmented collections or translations within larger historical works. The biography by Baha al-Din ibn Shaddad is the closest contemporary account that functions as a primary source for understanding Saladin's life and actions.
